ground_truth_root_cause: Deploy SHA 5c20010b3f8a (2026-05-13T10:51:05Z) modified deploy/redis/redis.conf but omitted the 'maxmemory-policy allkeys-lru' directive. The prior policy had been applied only at runtime via CONFIG SET (not persisted to the config file). When the Redis node restarted as part of the deployment, it loaded the updated redis.conf which lacked the maxmemory-policy setting, causing Redis to fall back to its default of 'noeviction'. With noeviction, no keys are evicted when memory is full, causing Redis to reject all write commands once maxmemory (8192MB) was reached, breaking cart-service and session-service.
ground_truth_remediation: 1. Immediately run: redis-cli CONFIG SET maxmemory-policy allkeys-lru — this restores write availability within seconds by allowing key eviction. 2. Persist the fix by adding 'maxmemory-policy allkeys-lru' to deploy/redis/redis.conf so the setting survives future restarts. 3. Commit and deploy the corrected redis.conf. 4. Verify with: redis-cli CONFIG GET maxmemory-policy. 5. Going forward, enforce that any runtime CONFIG SET changes are simultaneously written to the config file to prevent recurrence.
